mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average signals an active monetary easing policy that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines relative to its 12-month moving average, or Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0% and is rising, it signals a tightening cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and rising, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate a weakening housing market that is a leading indicator of broader demand contraction, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in RSAFS and HOUST fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year window, or Rank IC for interaction term falls below 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.5%), a positive month-over-month change in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals labor market recovery that supports corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE>5.5% and PAYEMS increases, or Rank IC for PAYEMS in this regime falls below 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) relative to its 3-month moving average indicates a strengthening labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS increases relative to its 3-month moving average, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below its 12-month moving average by more than 1.5%, it signals a contraction in manufacturing output that reduces corporate investment and earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO falls below the threshold, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and an increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% signals a monetary policy response to inflation that typically leads to positive equity returns as the market anticipates growth support without excessive inflation, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of FEDFUNDS decline and CPIAUCSL > 3.0% fails to predict positive SPX returns in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC for interaction term falls below 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 growth rate > 2.5% and rising), a decline in residential investment (RSAFS) signals a cooling housing market that precedes a broader demand slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when GDPC1 growth > 2.5% and RSAFS declines, or Rank IC for RSAFS in this regime falls below 0.03.
